newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber pare limit gain, but close higher.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber pare limit gain, but close higher.

text.p: CME lumber futures failed to hold an early limit gain in May of $10.00 per tbf following the housing report, but closed higher based on the strong numbers in the report, traders said.

May bulged the daily limit to $371.60 per tbf early before slipping to close $7.90 per higher at $369.50. Other months also ended under best levels, up $0.40 to $4.70 with July up $4.30 at $365.50 per tbf.
May shot up the limit at the opening and was supported throughout the day following the bullishly construed housing report, they said.

The U.S. Commerce Department reported February housing starts up 12.2 percent to 1.528 million annual rate and revised January starts to up 0.7 pcercent from up 2.0 percent. February starts were well above the average early estimate of 1.45 million units.
Building permits were also up 3.0 percent in February from a revised 1.5 percent decline in January.

However, futures failed to hold limit gains as some traders questioned the report in light of the weakness in cash lumber. There was no shortage of lumber in February based on cash market trends, they said.
"If this is the best we can do in cash with housing starts up so much, what will happen when spring building is completed?" one trader asked.
Cash markets also showed little movement after the report and continued their recent slow trade.
"My cash guys were saying there was very little reaction to the housing numbers," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Bears were also saying that most of the increase in starts came from multi-family starts which use less lumber than single-family units, Schmaedick added.
